chunks: He said: Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, he said: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Makki narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, he said: Abdul Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to us, from Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Ya'la ibn Murrah, from his father, from his grandfather Ya'la ibn Murrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, saying to Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him:
'O Ali! You are the master of the people after me. So whoever obeys you has indeed obeyed me, and whoever disobeys you has indeed disobeyed me.'

key_terms.أطاع: Obeyed, followed; carries religious connotation of submission to divinely appointed authority
key_terms.عصى: Disobeyed, rebelled against; implies transgression against divine authority
key_terms.ولي: Wali - master, guardian, protector; denotes spiritual and political authority in Shia theology

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali being the master of the people after him?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Mufid, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) explicitly designates Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) as the wali (master/guardian) of the people after him. This narration, transmitted through the companion Ya'la ibn Murrah al-Thaqafi, equates obedience and disobedience to Ali with obedience and disobedience to the Prophet himself, underscoring the continuity of divine authority through the Imamate.
